title: The frontend's port list shows a misspelt "Teestort", a shouted "TILBURY", a "Portsmouth  Port" with a doubled space and "Port of Sheerness" twice under the same code; DR1 shows each of those places once and spelt correctly.

finding.frontend: Five of the 78 port names a user reads are malformed (src/server/app/services/_capture/fixtures/ports-of-entry.json:256-304). "Teesport" is spelt "Teestort". "Tilbury" is rendered "TILBURY" in capitals while two neighbouring entries read "Tilbury Port" and "Tilbury 2 Ro-Ro Terminal"; because the list is sorted by name, the capitals also throw it three rows away from them, above "Teesside International Airport". "Portsmouth  Port" carries two spaces between the words. Sheerness appears twice, both labelled "Port of Sheerness", under the codes "GBSHS" and "GB SHS" — the same code with and without its space, so the two options differ on screen by nothing but that space. And Pembroke appears twice, both labelled "Pembroke Port", under "GB PED" and "GB PEM".
finding.prototype: DR1's port list carries "Teesport - GBTEE", "Tilbury - GBTIL" and "Sheerness - GBSHS", each spelt in sentence case and each appearing once, and carries no Pembroke or Portsmouth entry at all (app/views/arrival-details.html:67).
finding.difference: Correct the five labels: spell Teesport, put Tilbury in sentence case, remove the doubled space in Portsmouth Port, and collapse the duplicate Sheerness and Pembroke rows onto one code each. This is a data fix, not a page change, and it does not land in the frontend. The list is fetched at runtime from the reference-data service (src/server/app/services/ports/client.js), which serves it straight from DEFRA's master data (PortsOfEntryController -> MdmService in trade-imports-reference-data); the copy committed under the frontend's _capture fixtures is only the stub seed, so editing it corrects the local stack and nothing else. Raise the corrections against the master data. Worth doing whichever way the wider question about the port list is settled, though if that question replaces the dataset outright it goes with it.
finding.falsifiedBy: Finding "Teestort", "TILBURY", a second "Port of Sheerness" or a second "Pembroke Port" in DR1's port list, which would make these shared defects rather than frontend ones — DR1's list contains none of them.
finding.verification: Checked every quoted string character by character against the captured DOM rather than the source, and corrected none of them. grep of fe-arrival-details.html returns "Teestort", "TILBURY", "Port of Sheerness (GBSHS)" and "Port of Sheerness (GB SHS)" as written; an od -c dump of the Portsmouth option reads P o r t s m o u t h SP SP P o r t ( G B SP P M E ), confirming the doubled space between the words and a single space inside the code. The strings are identical in the source fixture at :254-306. Ran the falsifier against DR1's 213-entry list: it holds "Teesport - GBTEE", "Tilbury - GBTIL" and one "Sheerness - GBSHS", so it does not fire. The malformed data is the finding and it stands. Rubric 5 fires (a fifth instance was missed) and rubric 2 fires on one phrase; the band was also wrong. All three recorded in correction.
finding.correction: Missed: a fifth instance of the same defect. "Pembroke Port" appears twice in the frontend's list, at ports-of-entry.json:184 and :188, under "GB PED" and "GB PEM" — the same duplicate-place shape as Sheerness. Checked by grepping the fixture for Pembroke and reading both records. Added to finding.frontend and to the work in finding.difference, and "Four of the 78" corrected to "Five". Overstated: the two Sheerness rows were described as "indistinguishable on screen". They render as "Port of Sheerness (GBSHS)" and "Port of Sheerness (GB SHS)" and so do differ, by one space inside the code; the sentence has been narrowed to say that rather than struck. Wrongly banded: claimed `frontend-work` on the reading that the fixture under _capture is the data. True: services/ports/index.js serves the fixture only in stub mode and otherwise calls fetchPortsOfEntry against the reference-data service, whose PortsOfEntryController reads from MdmService, so the malformed strings originate in master data upstream of both repos and a fixture edit would be overwritten by the next capture. Checked by reading services/ports/index.js, client.js, _capture/capture.js and the reference-data controller. Rebanded to `needs-backend` and finding.difference now names where the fix has to be made.

relatedTo.why: both change the same port dataset
